title: plotdown block
description: A fenced plot block (plot, oplot or observable-plot): the options of Observable Plot's Plot.plot() as strict JSON, with marks and transforms as data. Spec version 0.1, generated from @observablehq/plot 0.6.19.

$schema.description: Optional URL of this schema, for editors.

data.description: Named datasets that marks refer to by name.

inset.description: Shorthand to set the same default for all four insets: **insetTop**, **insetRight**, **insetBottom**, and **insetLeft**.

insetTop.description: Insets the top edge by the specified number of pixels.

insetRight.description: Insets the right edge by the specified number of pixels.

insetBottom.description: Insets the bottom edge by the specified number of pixels.

insetLeft.description: Insets the left edge by the specified number of pixels.

clamp.description: If true, values below the domain minimum are treated as the domain minimum, and values above the domain maximum are treated as the domain maximum.

nice.description: If true, or a tick count or interval, extend the domain to nice round values.

round.description: If true, round the output value to the nearest integer (pixel); useful for crisp edges when rendering.

align.description: How to distribute unused space in the **range** for *point* and *band* scales.

padding.description: For *band* scales, how much of the **range** to reserve to separate adjacent bands; defaults to 0.1 (10%).

axis.description: The side of the frame on which to place the implicit axis: *top* or *bottom* for *x* or *fx*, or *left* or *right* for *y* or *fy*.

grid.description: Whether to show a grid aligned with the scale’s ticks.

legend.description: If true, produces a legend for the scale.

label.description: A textual label to show on the axis or legend; if null, show no label.

labelArrow.description: Whether to apply a directional arrow such as → or ↑ to the scale label.

width.description: The outer width of the plot in pixels, including margins.

height.description: The outer height of the plot in pixels, including margins.

aspectRatio.description: The desired aspect ratio of the *x* and *y* scales, affecting the default height.

margin.description: Shorthand to set the same default for all four margins: **marginTop**, **marginRight**, **marginBottom**, and **marginLeft**.

marginTop.description: The top margin; the distance in pixels between the top edges of the inner and outer plot area.

marginRight.description: The right margin; the distance in pixels between the right edges of the inner and outer plot area.

marginBottom.description: The bottom margin; the distance in pixels between the bottom edges of the inner and outer plot area.

marginLeft.description: The left margin; the distance in pixels between the left edges of the inner and outer plot area.

style.description: Custom styles to override Plot’s defaults.

className.description: The generated SVG element’s class name used for Plot’s default stylesheet; by default, a random string prefixed with “plot-”.

figure.description: Whether to wrap the generated SVG element with an HTML figure element.

ariaLabel.description: The [aria-label attribute][1] on the SVG root.

ariaDescription.description: The [aria-description attribute][1] on the SVG root.

clip.description: How to clip the mark; one of: - *frame* or true - clip to the plot’s frame (inner area) - *sphere* - clip to the projected sphere (*e.g.*, front hemisphere) - geojson - a GeoJSON object, typically with polygonal geometry - null or false - do not clip The *sphere* clip option requires a geographic projection.

x.description: Options for the horizontal position *x* scale.

y.description: Options for the vertical position *y* scale.

r.description: Options for the radius (size) *r* scale for dots or Point geos.

color.description: Options for the *color* scale for fill or stroke.

opacity.description: Options for the *opacity* scale for fill or stroke opacity.

symbol.description: Options for the categorical *symbol* scale for dots.

length.description: Options for the *length* scale for vectors.

projection.description: Options for projection; one of: - a named built-in projection such as *albers-usa* - a projection implementation, implementing the projection.*stream* method - a function that returns a projection implementation - a projection options object - null, for no projection A projection is an alternative to the *x* and *y* scales for encoding position, and is typically used to convert polygonal geometry in spherical coordinates to a planar visual representation.

fx.description: Options for the horizontal facet position *fx* scale.

fy.description: Options for the vertical facet position *fy* scale.

facet.description: Options for faceting, including shorthand options for the *fx* and *fy* facet scales and axes, and top-level faceting as an alternative to mark-level *fx* and *fy* channels.

marks.description: The marks to draw, in order: each is {"mark": name, "data": …, …options}.

anchor.description: The side of the frame on which to place the axis: *top* or *bottom* for horizontal axes (axisX and axisFx) and their associated vertical grids (gridX and gridFx), or *left* or *right* for vertical axes (axisY and axisFY) and their associated horizontal grids (gridY and gridFy).

ariaHidden.description: The [aria-hidden][1] state; a constant indicating whether the element is exposed to an accessibility API.

ariaLabel.description: The [aria-label][1]; a channel specifying short textual labels representing the value in the accessibility tree.

autoMark.description: The auto mark's own mark option (written autoMark because mark names the plotdown mark).

bandwidth.description: The bandwidth, a number in pixels which defaults to 20, specifies the standard deviation of the Gaussian kernel used for density estimation.

bend.description: The angle, a constant in degrees, between the straight line intersecting the arrow’s two control points and the outgoing tangent direction of the arrow from the start point.

binWidth.description: The distance between centers of neighboring hexagons, in pixels; defaults to 20.

blur.description: A non-negative pixel radius for smoothing; defaults to 0.

channels.description: An object defining additional custom channels.

ci.description: The confidence interval in (0, 1), or 0 to hide bands; defaults to 0.95.

clip.description: How to clip the mark; one of: - *frame* or true - clip to the plot’s frame (inner area) - *sphere* - clip to the projected sphere (*e.g.*, front hemisphere) - geojson - a GeoJSON object, typically with polygonal geometry - null or false - do not clip The *sphere* clip option requires a geographic projection.

color.description: Shorthand for setting both the fill and the stroke.

colorSpace.description: The [color space][1] of the backing canvas.

cumulative.description: If false or zero (default), produce a frequency distribution; if true or a positive number, produce a cumulative distribution; if a negative number, produce a [complementary cumulative][1] distribution.

curve.description: The curve (interpolation) method for connecting adjacent points.

delimiter.description: The path separator, used for inferring the hierarchy from the **path** channel; defaults to forward slash (/).

domain.description: The domain of allowed values; optional.

dot.description: Whether to represent the node with a dot; defaults to true unless a **marker** is specified.

dx.description: The horizontal offset in pixels; a constant option.

dy.description: The vertical offset in pixels; a constant option.

facet.description: Whether to enable or disable faceting; one of: - *auto* (default) - automatically determine if this mark should be faceted - *include* (or true) - draw the subset of the mark’s data in the current facet - *exclude* - draw the subset of the mark’s data *not* in the current facet - *super* - draw this mark in a single frame that covers all facets - null (or false) - repeat this mark’s data across all facets (*i.e.*, no faceting) When a mark uses *super* faceting, it is not allowed to use position scales (*x*, *y*, *fx*, or *fy*); *super* faceting is intended for decorations, such as labels and legends.

facetAnchor.description: How to place the mark with respect to facets; one of: - null (default for most marks) - display the mark in each non-empty facet - *top*, *right*, *bottom*, or *left* - display the mark only in facets on the given side - *top-empty*, *right-empty*, *bottom-empty*, or *left-empty* (default for axis marks) - display the mark only in facets that have empty space on the given side: either the margin, or an empty facet - *empty* - display the mark in empty facets only

fill.description: The [fill][1]; a constant CSS color string, or a channel typically bound to the *color* scale.

fillOpacity.description: The [fill-opacity][1]; a constant number between 0 and 1, or a channel typically bound to the *opacity* scale.

filter.description: Applies a transform to filter the mark’s index according to the given channel values; only truthy values are retained.

fontFamily.description: The [font-family][1]; a constant; defaults to the plot’s font family, which is typically [*system-ui*][2].

fontSize.description: The [font size][1] in pixels; either a constant or a channel; defaults to the plot’s font size, which is typically 10.

fontStyle.description: The [font style][1]; a constant; defaults to the plot’s font style, which is typically *normal*.

fontVariant.description: The [font variant][1]; a constant; if the **text** channel contains numbers or dates, defaults to *tabular-nums* to facilitate comparing numbers; otherwise defaults to the plot’s font style, which is typically *normal*.

fontWeight.description: The [font weight][1]; a constant; defaults to the plot’s font weight, which is typically *normal*.

format.description: How channel values are formatted for display.

frameAnchor.description: The frame anchor specifies defaults for **x** and **y**, along with **textAnchor** and **lineAnchor**, based on the plot’s frame; it may be one of the four sides (*top*, *right*, *bottom*, *left*), one of the four corners (*top-left*, *top-right*, *bottom-right*, *bottom-left*), or the *middle* of the frame.

fx.description: The horizontal facet position channel, for mark-level faceting, bound to the *fx* scale.

fy.description: The vertical facet position channel, for mark-level faceting, bound to the *fy* scale.

gap.description: The gap in pixels between cells; defaults to 1.

geometry.description: A required channel for the geometry to render; defaults to identity, assuming *data* is a GeoJSON object or an iterable of GeoJSON objects.

headAngle.description: How pointy the arrowhead is, in degrees; a constant typically between 0° and 180°, and defaults to 60°.

headLength.description: The size of the arrowhead relative to the **strokeWidth**; a constant.

height.description: The height (number of rows) of the raster grid, in actual pixels.

href.description: Link of each element: a field name; the values must be http, https, mailto or relative URLs.

imageFilter.description: A CSS [filter][1]; a constant string used to adjust the rendering of images, such as *blur(5px)*.

inset.description: Shorthand to set the same default for **insetStart** and **insetEnd**.

insetBottom.description: Insets the bottom edge by the specified number of pixels.

insetEnd.description: The ending inset, a constant in pixels; defaults to 0.

insetLeft.description: Insets the left edge by the specified number of pixels.

insetRight.description: Insets the right edge by the specified number of pixels.

insetStart.description: The starting inset, a constant in pixels; defaults to 0.

insetTop.description: Insets the top edge by the specified number of pixels.

interpolate.description: The spatial interpolation method, when using *data* samples.

interval.description: How to subdivide the domain into discrete bins; a stricter alternative to the **thresholds** option allowing the use of shorthand numeric intervals; one of: - an object that implements *floor*, *offset*, and *range* methods - a named time interval such as *day* (for date intervals) - a number (for number intervals), defining intervals at integer multiples of *n* For example, for integer bins: ```js Plot.rectY(numbers, Plot.binX({y: "count"}, {interval: 1})) ```

k.description: The number of standard deviations to offset the bands; defaults to 2.

label.description: A textual label to show on the axis or legend; if null, show no label.

labelAnchor.description: Where to place the axis **label** relative to the plot’s frame.

labelArrow.description: Whether to apply a directional arrow such as → or ↑ to the scale label.

labelOffset.description: The axis **label** position offset (in pixels); default depends on margins and orientation.

length.description: The vector’s length; either an optional channel bound to the *length* scale or a constant number in pixels.

lineAnchor.description: The line anchor controls how text is aligned (typically vertically) relative to its anchor point; it is one of *top*, *bottom*, or *middle*.

lineHeight.description: The line height in ems; defaults to 1.

lineWidth.description: The line width in ems (e.g., 10 for about 20 characters); defaults to infinity, disabling wrapping and clipping.

margin.description: Shorthand to set the same default for all four mark margins: **marginTop**, **marginRight**, **marginBottom**, and **marginLeft**; typically defaults to 0, except for axis marks.

marginBottom.description: The mark’s bottom margin; the minimum distance in pixels between the bottom edges of the inner and outer plot area.

marginLeft.description: The mark’s left margin; the minimum distance in pixels between the left edges of the inner and outer plot area.

marginRight.description: The mark’s right margin; the minimum distance in pixels between the right edges of the mark’s inner and outer plot area.

marginTop.description: The mark’s top margin; the minimum distance in pixels between the top edges of the inner and outer plot area.

marker.description: Shorthand to set the same default for markerStart, markerMid, and markerEnd; one of: - a marker name such as *arrow* or *circle* - *none* (default) - no marker * true - alias for *circle-fill* * false or null - alias for *none* * a function - a custom marker function; see below Custom marker functions are passed the current marker *color* and a *context* including the current document; they must return an SVG marker element.

markerEnd.description: The marker for the ending point of a line segment; one of: - a marker name such as *arrow* or *circle* * *none* (default) - no marker * true - alias for *circle-fill* * false or null - alias for *none* * a function - a custom marker function; see below Custom marker functions are passed the current marker *color* and a *context* including the current document; they must return an SVG marker element.

markerMid.description: The marker for any middle (interior) points of a line segment.

markerStart.description: The marker for the starting point of a line segment; one of: - a marker name such as *arrow* or *circle* * *none* (default) - no marker * true - alias for *circle-fill* * false or null - alias for *none* * a function - a custom marker function; see below Custom marker functions are passed the current marker *color* and a *context* including the current document; they must return an SVG marker element.

maxRadius.description: The maximum radius in pixels to determine whether to render the crosshair for closest point; if no point is within this radius to the pointer, the crosshair will be hidden.

mixBlendMode.description: The [mix-blend-mode][1]; a constant string specifying how to blend content such as *multiply*.

monospace.description: If true, changes the default **fontFamily** to *monospace*, and uses simplified monospaced text metrics calculations.

multiple.description: The number of cells per row or column; defaults to undefined for automatic.

n.description: The number of consecutive values in the window; defaults to 20.

negativeFill.description: The fill color when the primary value is less than the secondary value; defaults to blue.

negativeFillOpacity.description: The fill opacity when the primary value is less than the secondary value; defaults to **fillOpacity**.

offset.description: After stacking, an optional **offset** can be applied to translate and scale stacks, say to produce a streamgraph; defaults to null for a zero baseline (**y** = 0 for stackY, and **x** = 0 for stackX).

opacity.description: The [opacity][1]; a constant between 0 and 1, or a channel typically bound to the *opacity* scale.

order.description: The order in which stacks are layered; one of: - null (default) for input order - a named stack order method such as *inside-out* or *sum* - a field name, for natural order of the corresponding values - a function of data, for natural order of the corresponding values - an array of explicit **z** values in the desired order If the *wiggle* **offset** is used, as for a streamgraph, the default changes to *inside-out*.

paintOrder.description: The [paint-order][1]; a constant string specifying the order in which the **fill**, **stroke**, and any markers are drawn; defaults to *normal*, which draws the fill, then stroke, then markers; defaults to *stroke* for the text mark to create a “halo” around text to improve legibility.

path.description: The location of each node in the hierarchy; typically slash-separated strings, as with UNIX-based file systems or URLs.

pathFilter.description: The image filter for the tip’s box; defaults to a drop shadow.

pixelSize.description: The effective screen size of a raster pixel, used to determine the height and width of the raster from the frame’s dimensions; defaults to 1.

pointerEvents.description: The [pointer-events][1] property; a constant string such as *none*.

pointerSize.description: The size of the tip’s pointer in pixels; defaults to 12.

pool.description: Whether this mark participates in the pointer pool, which ensures that only the closest point is shown when multiple pointer marks are present; defaults to true for the tip mark.

positiveFill.description: The fill color when the primary value is greater than the secondary value; defaults to green.

positiveFillOpacity.description: The fill opacity when the primary value is greater than the secondary value; defaults to **fillOpacity**.

precision.description: The distance in pixels between samples of the confidence band; defaults to 4.

preferredAnchor.description: If an explicit tip anchor is not specified, an anchor is chosen automatically such that the tip fits within the plot’s frame; if the preferred anchor fits, it is chosen.

preserveAspectRatio.description: The image [aspect ratio][1]; defaults to *xMidYMid meet*.

r.description: The rounded radius for all corners, in pixels; shorthand for **rx1y1**, **rx2y1**, **rx2y2**, and **rx1y2**.

reduce.description: How to reduce **x** values when the **y** channel is binned with an **interval**; defaults to *first*.

reverse.description: Applies a transform to reverse the order of the mark’s index, say for reverse input order.

rotate.description: The rotation angle in degrees clockwise; a constant or a channel; defaults to 0°.

round.description: If true, round to integers to avoid partial cells.

rx.description: The rounded corner [*x*-radius][1], either in pixels or as a percentage of the rect width.

rx1.description: The rounded radius for the **x1** corners (typically left for positive *x*-values), in pixels; shorthand for **rx1y1** and **rx1y2**.

rx1y1.description: The rounded radius for the **x1y1** corner (typically bottom-left for positive values), in pixels.

rx1y2.description: The rounded radius for the **x1y2** corner (typically top-left for positive values), in pixels.

rx2.description: The rounded radius for the **x2** corners (typically right for positive *x*-values), in pixels; shorthand for **rx2y1** and **rx2y2**.

rx2y1.description: The rounded radius for the **x2y1** corner (typically bottom-right for positive values), in pixels.

rx2y2.description: The rounded radius for the **x2y2** corner (typically top-right for positive values), in pixels.

ry.description: The rounded corner [*y*-radius][1], either in pixels or as a percentage of the rect height.

ry1.description: The rounded radius for the **y1** corners (typically bottom for positive *y*-values), in pixels; shorthand for **rx1y1** and **rx2y1**.

ry2.description: The rounded radius for the **y2** corners (typically top for positive *y*-values), in pixels; shorthand for **rx1y2** and **rx2y2**.

shape.description: The shape of the vector; a constant.

shapeRendering.description: The [shape-rendering][1]; a constant string such as *crispEdges*.

smooth.description: Whether to apply linear interpolation after marching squares when computing contour polygons; defaults to true.

sort.description: Either applies a transform to sort the mark’s index by the specified channel values, or imputes ordinal scale domains from this mark’s channels.

src.description: Image URL: a field name or a constant URL. Images load from the network: they need the host to allow remote content.

strict.description: If true (the default), the output start values or end values or both (depending on the **anchor**) of each series may be undefined since there are not enough elements to create a window of size **n**; output values may also be undefined if some of the input values in the corresponding window are undefined.

stroke.description: The [stroke][1]; a constant CSS color string, or a channel typically bound to the *color* scale.

strokeDasharray.description: The [stroke-dasharray][1]; a constant number indicating the length in pixels of alternating dashes and gaps, or a constant string of numbers separated by spaces or commas (_e.g._, *10 2* for dashes of 10 pixels separated by gaps of 2 pixels), or *none* (the default) for no dashing [1]: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/SVG/Attribute/stroke-dasharray

strokeDashoffset.description: The [stroke-dashoffset][1]; a constant indicating the offset in pixels of the first dash along the stroke; defaults to zero.

strokeLinecap.description: The [stroke-linecap][1]; a constant specifying how to cap stroked paths, such as *butt*, *round*, or *square*.

strokeLinejoin.description: The [stroke-linejoin][1]; a constant specifying how to join stroked paths, such as *bevel*, *miter*, *miter-clip*, or *round*.

strokeMiterlimit.description: The [stroke-miterlimit][1]; a constant number specifying how to limit the length of *miter* joins on stroked paths.

strokeOpacity.description: The [stroke-opacity][1]; a constant between 0 and 1, or a channel typically bound to the *opacity* scale.

strokeWidth.description: The [stroke-width][1]; a constant number in pixels, or a channel.

sweep.description: The sweep order; defaults to 1 indicating a positive (clockwise) bend angle; -1 indicates a negative (anticlockwise) bend angle; 0 effectively clears the bend angle.

symbol.description: The categorical symbol; either a channel or a constant.

target.description: The [target][1]; a constant string specifying the target window (_e.g._, *_blank*) for clickable links; used in conjunction with the **href** option.

tension.description: The tension option only has an effect on bundle, cardinal and Catmull–Rom splines (*bundle*, *cardinal*, *cardinal-open*, *cardinal-closed*, *catmull-rom*, *catmull-rom-open*, and *catmull-rom-closed*).

text.description: The text contents channel, possibly with line breaks (\n, \r\n, or \r).

textAnchor.description: The [text anchor][1] controls how text is aligned (typically horizontally) relative to its anchor point; it is one of *start*, *end*, or *middle*.

textLayout.description: Layout for node labels: if *mirrored*, leaf-node labels are left-anchored, and non-leaf nodes right-anchored (with a -dx offset).

textOverflow.description: How truncate (or wrap) lines of text longer than the given **lineWidth**; one of: - null (default) - preserve overflowing characters (and wrap if needed) - *clip* or *clip-end* - remove characters from the end - *clip-start* - remove characters from the start - *ellipsis* or *ellipsis-end* - replace characters from the end with an ellipsis (…) - *ellipsis-start* - replace characters from the start with an ellipsis (…) - *ellipsis-middle* - replace characters from the middle with an ellipsis (…) If no **title** was specified, if text requires truncation, a title containing the non-truncated text will be implicitly added.

textPadding.description: The padding around the text in pixels; defaults to 8.

textStroke.description: The tick text **stroke**, say for a *white* outline to improve legibility; defaults to null.

textStrokeOpacity.description: The tick text **strokeOpacity**; defaults to 1; has no effect unless **textStroke** is set.

textStrokeWidth.description: The tick text **strokeWidth**; defaults to 4; has no effect unless **textStroke** is set.

thresholds.description: How to subdivide the domain into discrete bins; defaults to *auto*; one of: - a named threshold implementation such as *auto* (default) or *sturges* - a function that returns an array, count, or range interval - a range interval - an array of *n* threshold values for *n* - 1 bins - a count representing the desired number of bins (a hint; not guaranteed) For example, for about ten bins: ```js Plot.rectY(numbers, Plot.binX({y: "count"}, {thresholds: 10})) ``` See also the **interval** option.

tickFormat.description: How to format inputs (abstract values) for axis tick labels; one of: - a [d3-format][1] string for numeric scales - a [d3-time-format][2] string for temporal scales - a function passed a tick *value* and *index*, returning a string [1]: https://d3js.org/d3-time [2]: https://d3js.org/d3-time-format

tickPadding.description: The distance between an axis tick mark and its associated text label (in pixels); often defaults to 3, but may be affected by **tickSize** and **tickRotate**.

tickRotate.description: The rotation angle of axis tick labels in degrees clocksize; defaults to 0.

ticks.description: The desired approximate number of axis ticks, or an explicit array of tick values, or an interval such as *day* or *month*.

tickSize.description: The length of axis tick marks in pixels; negative values extend in the opposite direction.

tickSpacing.description: The desired approximate spacing between adjacent axis ticks, affecting the default **ticks**; defaults to 80 pixels for *x* and *fx*, and 35 pixels for *y* and *fy*.

tip.description: Whether to generate a tooltip for this mark, and any tip options.

title.description: The title; a channel specifying accessible, short textual descriptions as strings (possibly with newlines).

transform.description: Transforms applied in order: the first entry transforms the mark's options, the next one transforms the result.

treeAnchor.description: How to orient the tree; one of: - *left* (default) - place the root on the left, with children extending right - *right* - place the root on the right, with children extending left Use the **insetLeft** and **insetRight** *x* scale options if horizontal padding is desired, say to make room for labels.

treeLayout.description: How to layout the tree; defaults to [d3.tree][1] which implements the Reingold–Tilford “tidy” algorithm.

treeSeparation.description: How much space to reserve between adjacent nodes in the layout; by default, non-siblings are at least twice as far apart as siblings.

treeSort.description: How to order nodes prior to laying them out; by default, nodes are laid out in input order.

unit.description: The quantity each cell represents; defaults to 1.

value.description: The value can be specified as a channel based on the sample *data*, or as a function *f*(*x*, *y*) to be evaluated at each pixel if the *data* is not provided.

weight.description: An optional weight channel specifying the relative contribution of each point.

width.description: The width (number of columns) of the raster grid, in actual pixels.

x.description: The horizontal position (or length) channel, typically bound to the *x* scale.

x1.description: The required primary (starting, often left) horizontal position channel, representing the area’s baseline, typically bound to the *x* scale.

x2.description: The optional secondary (ending, often right) horizontal position channel, representing the area’s topline, typically bound to the *x* scale; if not specified, **x1** is used.

y.description: The vertical position channel, typically bound to the *y* scale; defaults to the zero-based index of the data [0, 1, 2, …].

y1.description: The required primary (starting, often bottom) vertical position channel, representing the area’s baseline, typically bound to the *y* scale.

y2.description: The optional secondary (ending, often top) vertical position channel, representing the area’s topline, typically bound to the *y* scale; if not specified, **y1** is used.

z.description: The **z** channel defines the series of each value in the stack.

mark.description: The name of the Plot mark, e.g. "dot" for Plot.dot.

data.description: The mark's data: an array of rows, the name of a dataset of the top-level data map, CSV or TSV text, a URL or GeoJSON.

transform.description: A transform: an object with one key, the transform's name, whose value is the transform's first argument.

channel.description: A channel: a field name (string), a constant (number, boolean, null; a CSS color for fill and stroke), an array of values, or an object {value, label, scale, …}. Strings that look like JavaScript functions are rejected.

interval.description: An interval: a number, or a time interval name such as "day", "week", "month", "3 months", "10 years".

markSort.description: Sorts the data (a field name, or {channel, order}), or sorts the domain of a scale by a channel ({"x": "-y", "reduce": …, "limit": …}).

inset.description: Shorthand to set the same default for all four insets: **insetTop**, **insetRight**, **insetBottom**, and **insetLeft**.

insetTop.description: Insets the top edge by the specified number of pixels.

insetRight.description: Insets the right edge by the specified number of pixels.

insetBottom.description: Insets the bottom edge by the specified number of pixels.

insetLeft.description: Insets the left edge by the specified number of pixels.

clamp.description: If true, values below the domain minimum are treated as the domain minimum, and values above the domain maximum are treated as the domain maximum.

nice.description: If true, or a tick count or interval, extend the domain to nice round values.

round.description: If true, round the output value to the nearest integer (pixel); useful for crisp edges when rendering.

align.description: How to distribute unused space in the **range** for *point* and *band* scales.

padding.description: For *band* scales, how much of the **range** to reserve to separate adjacent bands; defaults to 0.1 (10%).

axis.description: The side of the frame on which to place the implicit axis: *top* or *bottom* for *x* or *fx*, or *left* or *right* for *y* or *fy*.

grid.description: Whether to show a grid aligned with the scale’s ticks.

legend.description: If true, produces a legend for the scale.

label.description: A textual label to show on the axis or legend; if null, show no label.

labelArrow.description: Whether to apply a directional arrow such as → or ↑ to the scale label.

type.description: The scale type, affecting how the scale encodes abstract data, say by applying a mathematical transformation.

domain.description: The extent of the scale’s inputs (abstract values).

range.description: The extent of the scale’s outputs (visual values).

unknown.description: The scale’s output (visual value) when the input is invalid; defaults to null.

reverse.description: Whether to reverse the scale’s encoding; equivalent to reversing either the **domain** or **range**.

interval.description: Enforces uniformity for data at regular intervals, such as integer values or daily samples.

percent.description: If true, shorthand for a **transform** suitable for percentages, mapping proportions in [0, 1] to [0, 100].

scheme.description: If specified, shorthand for setting the **range** or **interpolate** option of a *color* scale.

exponent.description: A power scale’s exponent (*e.g.*, 0.5 for sqrt); defaults to 1 for a linear scale.

base.description: A log scale’s base; defaults to 10.

constant.description: A symlog scale’s constant, expressing the magnitude of the linear region around the origin; defaults to 1.

n.description: For a *quantile* scale, the number of quantiles (creates *n* - 1 thresholds); for a *quantize* scale, the approximate number of thresholds; defaults to 5.

pivot.description: For a diverging color scale, the input value (abstract value) that divides the domain into two parts; defaults to 0 for *diverging* scales, dividing the domain into negative and positive parts; defaults to 1 for *diverging-log* scales.

symmetric.description: For a diverging color scale, if true (the default), extend the domain to ensure that the lower part of the domain (below the **pivot**) is commensurate with the upper part of the domain (above the **pivot**).

paddingInner.description: For a *band* scale, how much of the range to reserve to separate adjacent bands.

paddingOuter.description: For a *band* scale, how much of the range to reserve to inset first and last bands.

ticks.description: The desired approximate number of axis ticks, or an explicit array of tick values, or an interval such as *day* or *month*.

tickSize.description: The length of axis tick marks in pixels; negative values extend in the opposite direction.

tickSpacing.description: The desired approximate spacing between adjacent axis ticks, affecting the default **ticks**; defaults to 80 pixels for *x* and *fx*, and 35 pixels for *y* and *fy*.

tickPadding.description: The distance between an axis tick mark and its associated text label (in pixels); often defaults to 3, but may be affected by **tickSize** and **tickRotate**.

tickFormat.description: How to format inputs (abstract values) for axis tick labels; one of: - a [d3-format][1] string for numeric scales - a [d3-time-format][2] string for temporal scales - a function passed a tick *value* and *index*, returning a string [1]: https://d3js.org/d3-time [2]: https://d3js.org/d3-time-format

tickRotate.description: The rotation angle of axis tick labels in degrees clocksize; defaults to 0.

fontVariant.description: The font-variant attribute for axis ticks; defaults to *tabular-nums* for quantitative axes.

ariaLabel.description: A short label representing the axis in the accessibility tree.

ariaDescription.description: A textual description for the axis in the accessibility tree.

labelAnchor.description: Where to place the axis **label** relative to the plot’s frame.

labelOffset.description: The axis **label** position offset (in pixels); default depends on margins and orientation.

line.description: If true, draw a line along the axis; if false (default), do not.

width.description: The width of the legend in pixels.

columns.description: The [CSS columns property][1], for a multi-column layout.

swatchSize.description: The swatch width and height in pixels; defaults to 15.

swatchWidth.description: The swatch width in pixels; defaults to **swatchSize**.

swatchHeight.description: The swatch height in pixels; defaults to **swatchSize**.

height.description: The height of the legend in pixels; defaults to 44 plus **tickSize**.

marginTop.description: The top margin in pixels; defaults to 18.

marginRight.description: The right margin in pixels; defaults to 0.

marginBottom.description: The bottom margin in pixels; defaults to 16 plus **tickSize**.

marginLeft.description: The left margin in pixels; defaults to 0.

opacity.description: The desired opacity of the color swatches or ramp; defaults to 1.

color.description: The constant color the ramp; defaults to black.

fill.description: The desired fill color of symbols; use *color* for a redundant encoding.

fillOpacity.description: The desired fill opacity of symbols; defaults to 1.

stroke.description: The desired stroke color of symbols; use *color* for a redundant encoding.

strokeOpacity.description: The desired stroke opacity of symbols; defaults to 1.

strokeWidth.description: The desired stroke width of symbols; defaults to 1.5.

r.description: The desired radius of symbols in pixels; defaults to 4.5.

output.description: An output of a bin, group or hexbin transform: a reducer name, or {reduce, scale, label}.

transformInputKey.description: Options that a transform reads from the mark's options; only valid when the mark has that transform.

inset.description: Shorthand to set the same default for all four insets: **insetTop**, **insetRight**, **insetBottom**, and **insetLeft**.

insetTop.description: Insets the top edge by the specified number of pixels.

insetRight.description: Insets the right edge by the specified number of pixels.

insetBottom.description: Insets the bottom edge by the specified number of pixels.

insetLeft.description: Insets the left edge by the specified number of pixels.

type.description: The desired projection; one of: - a named built-in projection such as *albers-usa* - a function that returns a projection implementation - null, for no projection When specified as a name, the projection is scaled and translated to fit the **domain** to the plot’s frame (minus insets).

domain.description: A GeoJSON object to fit to the plot’s frame (minus insets); defaults to a Sphere for spherical projections (outline of the whole globe).

rotate.description: A rotation of the sphere before projection; defaults to [0, 0, 0].

clip.description: The projection’s clipping method; one of: - *frame* or true (default) - clip to the plot’s frame (including margins but not insets) - a number - clip to a circle of the given radius in degrees centered around the origin - null or false - do not clip Some projections (such as [*armadillo*][1] and [*berghaus*][2]) require spherical clipping: in that case set the marks’ **clip** option to *sphere*.

x.description: x channel for top-level faceting; implies fx scale

y.description: y channel for top-level faceting; implies fy scale

margin.description: Shorthand to set the same default for all four facet margins: marginTop, marginRight, marginBottom, and marginLeft.

marginTop.description: The top facet margin; the (minimum) distance in pixels between the top edges of the inner and outer plot area.

marginRight.description: The right facet margin; the (minimum) distance in pixels between the right edges of the inner and outer plot area.

marginBottom.description: The bottom facet margin; the (minimum) distance in pixels between the bottom edges of the inner and outer plot area.

marginLeft.description: The left facet margin; the (minimum) distance in pixels between the left edges of the inner and outer plot area.

grid.description: Default axis grid for fx and fy scales; typically set to true to enable.

label.description: Default axis label for fx and fy scales; typically set to null to disable.

rows.description: Inline rows: objects, numbers, strings, booleans, null or arrays. A column made only of ISO 8601 date strings becomes dates.

anyOf.description: CSV text with a header row; values are typed (numbers, booleans, empty → null, ISO dates).
TSV text with a header row; typed as CSV.
A remote file. Only loaded when the host allows remote data.
The name of a dataset of the top-level data map.
